ai.description: *Lycodon flavomaculatus* is a slender snake reaching 60 cm. It is dark brown with distinct yellow spots or crossbands and a white belly. A key feature is its flattened head and enlarged fangs.
ai.identificationRemarks: The most reliable diagnostic feature of *Lycodon flavomaculatus* is the presence of distinct, bright yellow or white spots along the vertebral line, contrasting with its dark body.
ai.habitat: The Yellow-spotted Wolf Snake inhabits moist deciduous forests and scrublands in the Indian subcontinent, typically found at elevations between 300 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Yellow-spotted Wolf Snake is primarily nocturnal, emerging after dark to actively hunt for small lizards and their eggs among rocky crevices and forest floors.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lycodon flavomaculatus* is oviparous, typically laying clutches of 3–5 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing shortly thereafter.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Lycodon flavomaculatus* is endemic to peninsular India, primarily inhabiting the Western Ghats and surrounding regions at elevations ranging from sea level to 1,200 meters.
